title: Improvement Registry shard-write + deterministic compaction transaction

source_provenance.notes: Founder-authorized next engineering tranche selected atomic registry mutation and regression

problem_or_opportunity: The monolithic registry is unsafe for concurrent whole-file writes. The current family pointer solved visibility of extensions but still needs a canonical shard-write transaction and reproducible compaction path.
proposed_mechanism: Use candidate shards as the concurrent write surface; validate lifecycle/provenance and unique IDs across family; require optional expected-family SHA for stale-base protection; snapshot exact pre-write bytes; atomically write shard and family pointer; read back; automatically rollback on post-snapshot failure; provide explicit byte-preserving rollback; periodically compile base+extensions into deterministic canonical JSON plus an input/output hash manifest.
expected_benefit: Reduces lost-update risk, avoids risky reconstruction of a minified monolith, gives repeatable stale-write and duplicate-ID behavior, and makes registry compaction auditable/reversible.
pilot_evidence: Current SI-0008/0009/0010/0011/0012 extension architecture demonstrates shard visibility without rewriting base
H01-H02 deterministic fixture design covers commit/no-op, duplicate-ID conflict, malformed lifecycle, stale-base, interruption rollback, explicit rollback and deterministic compaction roundtrip
red_team_findings: Family pointer update itself remains subject to repository stale-write/rebase semantics
A process-local lock is not a distributed provider lease and must not be represented as one
Compactor must never silently override duplicate IDs
Compacted monolith is a build/read model, not proof that candidates are promoted
Unit/CI success is INTERNAL_EVIDENCE and does not replace a real registry transaction pilot
next_action: Run repository CI and then execute one real non-canon registry transaction through the new tool with GitHub readback; only after that consider PILOT_PASS/promotion.
notes: Pilot-ready engineering candidate only. Current registry-family architecture remains CURRENT; this candidate does not replace it until real pilot and promotion gates pass.
